extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS conference reviewers (assigned paper reviewers and area chairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for reviewing NeurIPS submissions, describing reviewer responsibilities, review-form fields, scoring rubrics (overall and confidence), and procedural requirements (conflict checking, confidentiality, discussion, author response).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are assigned ~4-6 submissions and are responsible for reviewing submissions, reading and responding to author responses, participating in discussion with other reviewers and ACs, and helping make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and meta-reviews will be made public after decisions (identities remain anonymous). If a reviewer cannot review a paper they should notify the AC promptly so an alternate can be found. Engage actively in the discussion phase even if not prompted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect deadlines and respond to emails promptly; check spam for CMT emails and keep CMT profile/contact info up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unavailable for more than a short period (especially during important windows like discussion), inform ACs. Do not reply directly to CMT emails; use CMT's 'email meta-reviewer' links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon assignment, log into CMT to check for conflicts and ensure the paper falls within your expertise; notify AC immediately if you are uncomfortable reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep domain conflicts in CMT up to date; fill out a note in CMT to request reassignment when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything related to the review process confidential. Do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until they are public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not distribute submissions (code or results) to anyone without program chairs' approval. Code submitted for review cannot be distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing is double blind at the level of reviewers and ACs; authors must anonymize submissions and reviewers must not attempt to discover author identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is not adequately anonymized, contact the AC. If you accidentally discover identities, do not divulge them and do not let them influence your decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit up to 100MB of supplementary material (PDF or ZIP). Reviewer's primary responsibility is to review the submission itself; consulting supplementary material is discretionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because NeurIPS submissions are short, reviewers may wish to consult supplementary materials before criticizing lack of details, proofs, or experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executing submitted code and clicking links safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted code may contain vulnerabilities; exercise caution when executing or following links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If running code, use secure environments (Docker container, VM, or network-isolated cloud instance). Be cautious about web links that may log IPs or contain vulnerabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and page limit compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are limited to eight content pages (including figures/tables) in the NeurIPS submission style; discussion of broader impact and references may be on additional pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must use the NeurIPS 2020 LaTeX style file. If assigned a paper that violates style or page limits, notify the AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers identical or substantially similar to submissions to other archival venues or to other NeurIPS submissions are considered dual submissions and should be treated as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slicing contributions too thinly may cause dual-submission determination. If suspected, contact the corresponding AC. See Call for Papers and FAQ for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content: general standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be detailed, informative, and constructive; short or superficial reviews that express uninformed opinions are worse than no review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews inform decisions and help authors improve. Include thorough explanations, cite prior work precisely when needed, and avoid dismissive or inappropriate language. Be fair and help authors understand your viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and contributions (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper motivation, key contributions and achievements in a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps ACs and authors identify misunderstandings; indicate main contributions (theoretical, methodological, empirical, bridging fields, critical analysis). See Examples of Review Content for sample phrasings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strengths of the work; typical criteria include soundness of claims, empirical evaluation, significance, novelty, and relevance to the NeurIPS community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List strengths concretely (e.g., theoretical correctness, experimental validation, scalability, novelty). Cite relevant prior works precisely when comparing significance or novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weaknesses (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the limitations of the work along axes similar to strengths (soundness, significance, novelty, relevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be detailed, specific, polite; avoid vague subjective complaints. Treat weaknesses as constructive feedback and explain how they affect the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claims and methods are correct and whether the empirical methodology is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify incorrect claims or methodological issues specifically and politely; such problems are primary grounds for rejection and should be thoroughly motivated so authors can respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the paper is well written and clearly organized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give examples of parts needing revision and concrete suggestions to improve exposition. A well-written paper should provide enough information for an expert to reproduce results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to prior work (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether the submission clearly situates itself relative to previous contributions and explains differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related work should not be a list; it should explain how the proposed work differs. Authors are excused for not citing very recent non-refereed work (<2 months before deadline) but should address contemporaneous work appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (review form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether there are enough details to reproduce the major results of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reproducibility is insufficient, list it among the weaknesses. Consider whether supplementary materials contain necessary details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional feedback, suggestions, and questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide any extra comments, suggestions for improvement, or specific questions for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this field for actionable guidance (e.g., request experiment X be run, ask for parameter settings) and for constructive suggestions to improve the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (review form item and mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: An overall numeric score reflecting assessment of the submission's contribution; do not normalize to conference acceptance rate or assume assignments are representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale guidance: 10 = Top 5% of accepted NeurIPS papers (groundbreaking); 9 = Top 15% accepted (excellent); 8 = Top 50% accepted (very good); 7 = good (accept); 6 = marginally above threshold; 5 = marginally below threshold; 4 = okay but reject; 3 = clear reject; 2 = strong reject (surprised it was submitted); 1 = trivial/wrong/already known. Choose the score to reflect contribution level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (review form item and mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1–5 confidence rating indicating how certain you are about your assessment and familiarity with the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5 = absolutely certain/very familiar; 4 = confident but not absolute; 3 = fairly confident (math/details not carefully checked); 2 = willing to defend but likely unfamiliar with central parts; 1 = educated guess, not in your area or hard to understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader impact adequacy (broader impact section assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the authors adequately addressed potential ethical and societal implications (Yes/No/Only partially).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should discuss both positive and negative outcomes. Reviewers should evaluate whether the broader impact statement is adequate and balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag whether the submission raises potential ethical concerns (methods, applications, or data that create/reinforce unfair bias or aim for harm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer yes/no and briefly explain. This flag is independent of your rating; if AC shares concern, specialized ethics reviewers may be assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous reviewing/resubmission history
rubrics_metrics.description: Report whether you have previously reviewed or area chaired a version of this work for another archival venue (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps ACs put your review in context; ACs may access a resubmission statement from authors describing prior rejections and changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to abide by the NeurIPS Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must agree to follow the NeurIPS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link provided; adherence is required to serve as reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to area chair
rubrics_metrics.description: A text field for comments to the AC that should not be shown to authors (e.g., blunt comparisons to other submissions or identity-related notes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for material you wish kept from authors. If you accidentally discover author identities, note it here rather than exposing identities publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response handling responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must read author responses and update their reviews or explicitly state why their opinion remains unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore author responses; indicate if you read them and explain whether you agree or disagree and why. Be specific rather than saying only 'my opinion remains the same.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion phase engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: After author responses, ACs initiate discussions to reach consensus; reviewers should participate constructively and consider other viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consensus is valued but not mandatory; be open to changing your assessment when convinced. Discussions are important for borderline/discordant submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer best practices and professional behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Be professional, polite, avoid discrimination and biased phrasing (e.g., avoid phrasing that implies non-native status), and do not divulge or discuss assigned submissions without AC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inappropriate comments (e.g., 'have your submission proof-read by a native English speaker' -> use 'please proof-read for English style and grammar issues'). Do not give in to undue influence; cite work precisely when needed; do not dismiss any submission without thorough reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC evaluation of review quality and incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will evaluate review quality with three scores: 'exceeded expectations', 'met expectations', and 'failed to meet expectations'; top reviewers receive registration incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The top 8% highest-scoring reviewers get free NeurIPS registrations; the next ~30% have registrations reserved. Low-scoring reviewers may not be invited in future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of review-quality axes (quality, originality, clarity, significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative evaluation axes used in example reviews: Quality (technical soundness), Originality (novelty of tasks/methods), Clarity (writing and organization), and Significance (impact and usefulness to community).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these axes to structure strengths/weaknesses and to justify overall score; examples of phrasing and typical reviewer comments are provided to guide what constitutes good/bad evaluations.
